title: What does EscrowCancel do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of EscrowCancel and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, EscrowCancel returns expired escrowed principal to the sender after the ledger's cancellation deadline. [1]

Passing CancelAfter makes cancellation possible; it does not automatically move money. Any account may submit the cancellation, identifying the original Owner and OfferSequence. An escrow without CancelAfter cannot be canceled this way. Transaction fees remain spent even when the full principal returns to its original owner. [1]

The EscrowCancel reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using EscrowCancel, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
